summary: The note collects family recipes and strategies for feeding picky eaters, centered on hiding vegetables in kid-friendly dishes such as nuggets, rice, bread, pasta and smoothies. It also covers involving children in cooking, making fish appealing, encouraging culinary adventure, and rewarding bravery with positive reinforcement. Each approach is illustrated with a named parent, expert or chef.
one_line: Family-tested hidden-veggie recipes and encouragement strategies that help parents win over picky eaters at mealtime.
key_facts: Charlotte Bennett, a dietitian and mother of two, makes 'Love Nuggets' from ground chicken breast blended with steamed carrots, broccoli and sweet potatoes, then bakes them; her son Alex is a discerning 7-year-old.
The Anderson family of suburban Cincinnati turned cauliflower into 'Snowy Rice' by mixing it with regular rice, peas and corn; Sara Anderson is a mother of three.
Michael Santiago created Zucchini Chocolate Chip Bread on December 3, 2023 to get his picky daughter to eat more greens.
The Williams family of Denver, Colorado uses spiralized zoodles and squash ribbons with wheat pasta and a tomato sauce containing pureed seasonal vegetables.
Jessica Cartwright, a single mother from Boston, makes 'Superhero Smoothies' of fruit with hidden spinach or kale, garnished with fresh berries, introduced in early September.
Child psychologist Dr. Liam Peterson wrote in an article dated October 22, 2023 that children who help choose and prepare food are more invested in eating it.
Making personal pizzas, where kids 'paint' sauce and choose vegetable toppings, is cited as a game-changing interactive strategy.

On November 17, 2023, Samuel Richardson, a fishing enthusiast and father, made 'Ocean Patties' of flaked salmon, bread crumbs and finely diced bell peppers shaped like fish, served with homemade tartar sauce.
Chef Chloe Taylor launched a kid-friendly international tasting menu on December 1, 2023, saying 'Food is a journey.'
Janet and Mark O'Connor use a 'Bravery Board' on which their kids earn stickers for being adventurous with food.
Charlotte Bennett was interviewed on October 5, 2023, and said vegetables should be a normal part of what children eat, not something dreaded.
